sources.title: Views and Queries: Determinacy and Rewriting
sources.authors: Alan Nash, Luc Segoufin, Victor Vianu
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction and formal definition on PDF pages 2 and 8; not a full-paper reproduction
sources.finding: View determinacy means equal view outputs imply equal query answers on all allowed database instances. It is distinguished from expressibility of a rewriting in a chosen language.
sources.overlap: Our equal-history/different-answer constructions are ordinary counterexamples to determinacy, not a new principle.
sources.caution: Do not transfer the paper's query-language-specific results automatically to full SQLite aggregates, NULL or bag semantics. An optimizer's failure to find a rewrite is not by itself a proof of insufficient information.

sources.title: Algorithms for Rewriting Aggregate Queries Using Views
sources.authors: Sara Cohen, Werner Nutt, Alexander Serebrenik
sources.read_scope: Title page, abstract and introduction; no implementation reproduced
sources.finding: Presents sound aggregate-view rewriting algorithms for count and sum, with completeness in specified cases and adaptations for min/max.
sources.overlap: Computing new aggregates from materialized old results is established database work, not an agent-specific invention.
sources.caution: This reading does not certify support for our exact SQLite queries, nor an arbitrary average/NULL rewrite. Keep implementation capability claims separate from mathematical derivability.

sources.title: Explaining Wrong Queries Using Small Examples
sources.authors: Zhengjie Miao, Sudeepa Roy, Jun Yang
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction and Section 2.1 problem definition
sources.finding: Given two queries differing on a database, seeks small constraint-respecting subinstances that retain the difference; develops provenance/solver-based algorithms and aggregate extensions.
sources.overlap: Small executable counterexamples for SQL explanation already have algorithmic prior art.
sources.difference: Our current two-database equal-view witnesses address result non-determination rather than minimizing a supplied single-database inequivalence example. That distinction alone does not establish novelty.

application_to_local_evidence.formula: For an explicitly declared constraint class K: a pair D1,D2 in K with V(D1)=V(D2) and Q(D1)!=Q(D2) refutes universal answer recovery from V alone over K.
application_to_local_evidence.local_evidence: cache-full-schema-witnesses-20261025-001 supplies two such finite pairs for the unchanged reference SQL under the pinned declared schemas.
not_proven: That a particular real cached value has multiple possible current answers; generic non-determinacy need not imply ambiguity for every view value
That the entire agent observation is identical between witness worlds: snapshot hashes and external facts are not part of the equal-view certificate
That no extra base-table query or additional metadata could answer the task
That the reference SQL matches the independently intended human request
That the agent used, misunderstood or ignored these mathematical facts
application_to_local_evidence.hash_boundary: A database fingerprint binds provenance. These certificates concern the historical result and declared relational constraints, not an information-theoretic analysis of every bit of provenance metadata or hidden model knowledge.

strong_baseline_semantic_states.requirement: Validated rewriting or proof under the explicitly scoped semantics; finite successful tests alone are not universal proof
strong_baseline_semantic_states.action: Reuse only with required completeness, version, typing and constraint checks
Reject a universal cache-only recovery claim; recompute or obtain missing information. Do not label every instance unrecoverable.

strong_baseline_semantic_states.requirement: No accepted proof or counterexample; optimizer timeout, unsupported operator or rewrite miss stays unknown
strong_baseline_semantic_states.action: Fallback while separately counting inability to certify; not scored as semantic insufficiency

novelty_gate.established: Reproducible task-relationship checks and a no-error/no-reuse development result
novelty_gate.not_established: Agent demand-drift phenomenon, an autonomous counterexample-search algorithm, or quality/cost gains over strong applicability checks plus recomputation
novelty_gate.next_needed: Independent semantics for candidate tasks, then a preapproved fixed development comparison. No method naming or broad novelty claim based only on these witnesses.
